task.title: Node.js Sandbox Deadlock Issue and Restart Solution

user_message.content:
Monthly Inspections Checklist Web App - Manus

Share
whats the hold up here?
The sandbox has a kernel-level filesystem I/O deadlock that's blocking Node.js entirely. Every time node starts, it gets stuck in an uninterruptible sleep (D-state) trying to load a system library — even a node -e "console.log('hello')" hangs. This is not something I can fix from inside the sandbox; it requires a full sandbox restart from the Manus platform side.
Here's the situation in plain terms:
What's broken
Why
Dev server (port 3000)
Node.js hangs on startup — every node process enters D-state
webdev_restart_server
Fails with "fetch failed" — the webdev service can't reach the dev server
webdev_save_checkpoint
Also fails — depends on git, which is also stuck in D-state
GitHub push
TLS to GitHub is blocked at the network level from this sandbox
The good news: All the code changes are already written and saved to disk. The tasks_data.json with 142 top-level tasks is in place. Everything is ready — the sandbox just can't run Node or git right now.
What would fix this immediately:
A full sandbox restart/reset from the Manus platform (not just a page refresh)
Can you try one of these?
Close this task session and start a new one — the sandbox should get a fresh environment
Look for a "Reset Sandbox" or "Restart Environment" option in the Manus UI
Let me know if there's a way to trigger a hard restart from your end
Once the sandbox is healthy, I can save the checkpoint and get the dev server running in under a minute.

The app is fully built and running. Here's what was delivered from scratch in this session:

The complete **Monthly Inspections Checklist** app is live — dark-mode slate/navy, single-page, no login required. All 4 tabs, sidebar, localStorage persistence, and print/PDF export are wired and working. 21 vitest tests pass with zero TypeScript errors.

**What's included:**
- **Sidebar** — Default Record + unlimited saved records; create, rename (modal), save-as (modal), delete; Enter/Escape keyboard support on all modals
- **Header** — Building selector (9 buildings), Unit #, Inspector/Manager name, custom date-time picker with a **Now** shortcut (local time, not UTC)
- **HQS Checklist** — 4 emergency items (red badge), 23 non-emergency items (2-column grid), timestamp + manager name on check, custom item add/remove, Web Audio click sound
- **Make Ready** — OK / Repair Required / Clean toggle buttons with timestamps, 9 categories, 40 items
- **Pre-Move-Out** — Work Needed dropdown (auto-stamps on "Yes"), Date/Vendor/Comments inputs, 7 categories, signature lines in print
- **Charge List** — 44 items across 9 categories, editable prices (format to $XX.XX on blur/Enter), running total, 3 regional pricing presets
- **Export** — Export PDF (current tab), Export All – Filled, Export All – Blank (hand-writable forms with underlines)

**Three suggested next steps:**

1. **Add your actual building list** — Replace the placeholder addresses in `client/src/lib/inspectionData.ts` under `BUILDINGS[]` with your real property addresses and regional manager assignments.

2. **Expand the Charge List pricing** — The `REGIONAL_PRESETS` object in `inspectionData.ts` currently has Standard, Downtown Premium, and Suburban. You can add presets per manager or region (e.g., "Beth Cohen – North", "Menowitz – South") with custom price overrides for each.

3. **Add a Notes/Photos field** — A free-text notes area per tab (or per record) would be a natural extension for field inspectors who need to capture observations that don't fit the structured checklist items.
